property_description: Each block of six solutions (pure salt A, four mixtures A+B, pure salt B) is mutually isopiestic at 25 C; 'm' is the total molality (mol of solute per kg water, both salts counted) of each solution, yB = mole fraction of salt B in the total solute (yB = 0 pure A, 1.0 pure B). No reference salt is separately designated in the table; the first row of a block (yB = 0) is the pure salt A solution, the last (yB = 1.0) the pure salt B solution.
pressure_note: not stated (isopiestic equilibrium at the vapour pressure of the solutions, in desiccators; no pressure printed)

value.what: total molality of the solution in isopiestic equilibrium with the other five solutions of its block

composition.other_species: salt pairs of NaCl, KCl, NaBr, KBr; bromides are outside the six-ion set (NaBr-KBr block is entirely out of scope, kept as the table mixes scope); salts A and B are set per block by the label row

skip_rows.reason: block label rows (salt pair and block number)

conversion_needs: molality of each salt = total m * (1 - yB) for A and total m * yB for B; vapour pressure/water activity of each block must come from the reference osmotic coefficient of pure salt A (not printed in this table)
notes: Stacked layout: the printed table has three (m, yB) column pairs side by side; the six pairs are in panels. Panels with fewer than three blocks (NaCl-KCl one block, NaCl-NaBr two blocks, NaCl-KBr two blocks) were identified by agreement of each block's mean molality of the mixed solutions with Table IV (3.549; 4.325 and 3.090; 4.268 and 2.891). Blocks stacked left to right; the 'block k of n' text only numbers them.
quality_remarks: Total molality m equals the ionic strength and yB equals the ionic-strength fraction only because all four salts (NaCl, KCl, NaBr, KBr) are 1-1; the rule is therefore valid here. No osmotic coefficient or water activity is printed in Table I (needs a reference-salt converter). Only the NaCl-KCl block and the pure NaCl/KCl rows are inside the six-ion set; the bromide blocks are held as outside the set.
